headline: Slow-bleed decade: debt creeps, blocs harden, a 2029 bond wobble reshapes fiscal politics

events: US extends sectoral tariffs to pharmaceuticals and machinery; EU and Canada retaliate narrowly, global trade volume growth slows to ~1.5%
Fed cuts to 3.25% then pauses as core inflation sticks near 3%; ECB holds at 2%
Ukraine front freezes into an unratified ceasefire line; reconstruction financing stalls over frozen-asset disputes
AI capex peaks; hyperscaler earnings disappoint, equity correction of ~15% in tech without broader recession
Ethiopia and Malawi restructurings drag on; Common Framework remains slow
US presidential election won narrowly on a populist cost-of-living platform; tariff revenue earmarked for household rebates
China growth slips to ~3.8% as property overhang persists; Beijing pushes export volumes into Global South, triggering anti-dumping duties in Brazil, India, Indonesia
Global growth dips to 2.4%; unemployment edges up as white-collar hiring freezes spread in services
Heatwaves in South Asia and Mediterranean set new records; insurers withdraw from more coastal and wildfire markets
Pakistan secures emergency IMF program after reserves fall below one month of imports
Weak US Treasury auctions push 10-year yield to 5.6%; a 'term-premium wobble' forces Fed to slow QT and Treasury to shift issuance to bills
Japan JGB yields above 2.5%; BoJ caps long end informally, yen weakens past 170
France faces a downgrade and snap election; spreads widen but ECB TPI talk calms markets
Egypt and Kenya enter debt distress; Egypt reprofiles domestic and Eurobond debt with Gulf backing
Limited Serbia-Kosovo armed clashes draw NATO peacekeeping reinforcement; the run's one major new conflict
Agentic AI tools spread in back-office functions; ~22% of firms use AI in production
Most 2030 climate targets publicly missed; COP35 produces a methane and grid pledge but no new finance; emissions edge down ~0.5%
US passes modest fiscal package: small spending caps paired with extended tax cuts, net deficit barely changes at ~6.5% of GDP
EU launches a second joint borrowing facility for defence, legitimising permanent common debt
Youth unemployment protests in Nigeria, Kenya and Bangladesh over fuel subsidy cuts and job scarcity
Global renewable share passes 40% on cheap Chinese solar and storage, while Western grids lag on transmission permitting
Global growth steadies near 2.8%; inflation settles around 3% with policy rates ~3.5%
Argentina seeks yet another reprofiling after peso pressure, the fourth sovereign crisis of the period
US-China agree a narrow chip-and-rare-earths 'managed trade' memorandum, but broad tariffs remain
AI productivity gains visible in software, finance and logistics statistics (~0.3pp/yr), while displaced clerical workers swell gig and care sectors
Housing affordability remains the top voter issue across OECD; several cities adopt rent caps and zoning upzoning in parallel

winners: India, Vietnam and Mexico as connector economies capturing diverted supply chains
Large AI platform and cloud firms with pricing power
losers: Indebted frontier economies in Africa and South Asia squeezed by high rates and aid cuts
Young renters and mid-skill clerical workers in advanced economies
Small export-dependent firms facing multiple incompatible tariff and compliance regimes
bullets: No crash, but a 2029 bond-market wobble reset the consensus that rich-country debt is costless; governments now issue shorter and pray for growth.
Global public debt crossed 100% of GDP; interest costs exceed defence spending in the US and several European states.
Trade runs through three overlapping blocs (US-aligned, China-centred, non-aligned connectors) with tariffs at their highest since the 1940s.
AI is mundane infrastructure in a third of firms; productivity gains are real but concentrated, and wage gains even more so.
Warming reached ~1.57C; climate adaptation spending quietly outpaces mitigation finance in budgets.
Four sovereign debt crises were managed piecemeal, each leaving austerity and youth discontent behind.
Trust in institutions drifted lower and unrest rose, expressed mostly through elections and cost-of-living protests rather than revolutions.
The Ukraine war is frozen rather than ended; the Middle East remains a chronic flashpoint with periodic shipping disruptions.
wildcard: Armed clashes between Serbia and Kosovo in 2029 required a NATO peacekeeping surge, briefly reviving fears of a wider Balkan war.
image_description: In a sweltering 2031 Lagos evening, a young delivery rider waits under a solar-lit kiosk, phone showing an AI dispatch app and a bank alert that fuel prices rose again, while a half-finished Chinese-built rail viaduct looms overhead.
